description: The benchmark is the average net fee rate over all matched fee records pooled together, so each fee record counts equally.

d.request: Calculate the overall average net fee rate as the mean of (feerate - rebrate) across all fees matched to orders by exact recordvault-orderslink equality; for each trading pair (mktnote), calculate its mean net fee rate from matched fees; identify pairs strictly above the overall average; return one row with the mean of those pairs' average rates and the mean excess per pair above the overall average, omitting missing values and without rounding.
d.sql: WITH fee_order_match AS (SELECT f.feerate, f.rebrate, o.mktnote, (f.feerate - f.rebrate) as net_fee_rate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(net_fee_rate) as overall_avg_net_rate FROM fee_order_match), pair_avg AS (SELECT mktnote, AVG(net_fee_rate) as pair_avg_net_rate FROM fee_order_match GROUP BY mktnote), pairs_above_avg AS (SELECT p.pair_avg_net_rate, (p.pair_avg_net_rate - oa.overall_avg_net_rate) as excess FROM pair_avg p CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE p.pair_avg_net_rate > oa.overall_avg_net_rate) SELECT AVG(pair_avg_net_rate) as mean_of_above_avg_pairs, AVG(excess) as mean_excess_above_overall_avg FROM pairs_above_avg

b.request: Trading pairs whose average net fee rate (feerate minus rebrate per pair) exceeds the overall average net fee rate calculated from all matched fee records (with each record weighted equally), returning the mean of those qualifying pairs' average net fee rates and the mean amount by which they individually exceed the overall average.
b.sql: WITH fee_net_rates AS (SELECT f.feesnode, f.feerate - f.rebrate as net_fee_rate, o.mktnote FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(net_fee_rate) as overall_avg_rate FROM fee_net_rates), pair_averages AS (SELECT mktnote, AVG(net_fee_rate) as pair_avg_rate FROM fee_net_rates GROUP BY mktnote), qualifying_pairs AS (SELECT pa.mktnote, pa.pair_avg_rate, oa.overall_avg_rate, pa.pair_avg_rate - oa.overall_avg_rate as excess FROM pair_averages pa CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE pa.pair_avg_rate > oa.overall_avg_rate) SELECT AVG(pair_avg_rate) as mean_of_qualifying_pairs, AVG(excess) as mean_excess FROM qualifying_pairs
b.raw: Trading pairs whose average net fee rate (feerate minus rebrate per pair) exceeds the overall average net fee rate calculated from all matched fee records (with each record weighted equally), returning the mean of those qualifying pairs' average net fee rates and the mean amount by which they individually exceed the overall average.

c.request: Using fee records matched to their orders (the order's `recordvault` equals the fee's `orderslink`, compared exactly as text; unmatched fees dropped), which trading pairs (`mktnote`, with records lacking a pair treated as one group) have an average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`) strictly above the overall average net fee rate? Give me one row for those pairs: the mean of their average net fee rate, and the mean amount by which they exceed the overall average. If the overall average is missing, no pairs count. Skip missing values in the averages (missing if there's nothing to average) and don't round anything. The benchmark is the average net fee rate over all matched fee records pooled together, so each fee record counts equally.
c.sql:
WITH matched_fees AS (
  SELECT f.feerate - f.rebrate as net_fee_rate, o.mktnote
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(net_fee_rate) as avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM matched_fees
),
pair_averages AS (
  SELECT mktnote, AVG(net_fee_rate) as avg_net_fee
  FROM matched_fees
  GROUP BY mktnote
),
qualifying_pairs AS (
  SELECT pa.avg_net_fee, oa.avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM pair_averages pa
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  WHERE oa.avg_net_fee_rate IS NOT NULL
    AND pa.avg_net_fee > oa.avg_net_fee_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_net_fee) as mean_of_averages,
  AVG(avg_net_fee - avg_net_fee_rate) as mean_excess
FROM qualifying_pairs

a.request: Match each fee record to its order (the order's `recordvault` equals the fee's `orderslink`, compared exactly as text), and leave out fee records with no matching order. Group the matched records by trading pair (`mktnote`), with records lacking a trading pair forming one group, and work out each pair's average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`). For the benchmark, take the average net fee rate over all matched fee records pooled together, with each fee record counting equally. Keep only the trading pairs whose average net fee rate is strictly above this benchmark (if the benchmark is missing, keep none), and return a single row with: the average of their average net fee rates, and the average amount by which they exceed the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average (an average with nothing to average is missing), and don't round the results.
a.sql:
WITH matched_fees AS (
  SELECT 
    f.feerate,
    f.rebrate,
    o.mktnote,
    (f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS net_fee_rate
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(net_fee_rate) AS benchmark_rate
  FROM matched_fees
  WHERE net_fee_rate IS NOT NULL
),
pair_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    mktnote,
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM matched_fees
  WHERE net_fee_rate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY mktnote
),
filtered_pairs AS (
  SELECT 
    pa.avg_net_fee_rate,
    pa.avg_net_fee_rate - b.benchmark_rate AS excess
  FROM pair_averages pa
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE b.benchmark_rate IS NOT NULL AND pa.avg_net_fee_rate > b.benchmark_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS avg_of_averages,
  AVG(excess) AS avg_excess
FROM filtered_pairs
